blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Job Analysis systematically gathers information about job responsibilities, duties, and required human qualifications.
Recruitment focuses on searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply for jobs in the organization.
Selection involves evaluating applicants through tests and interviews to choose the most suitable candidate.
E-Recruitment uses web-based channels, job portals, and applicant tracking systems (ATS) for hiring efficiency.
Onboarding and Induction ensure smooth transition and organizational socialisation for newly appointed staff.

blocks.content: Job Analysis is the process of collecting, analysing, and setting out information about the content of a job in order to provide a basis for job description, person specification, and recruitment. It is the foundation of all HR functions.

cells: Written statement of job title, duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships, working conditions, and performance standards
Recruitment; clarity of role; performance appraisal; legal compliance
Minimum qualifications, experience, skills, competencies, and attributes required for the job
Systematic comparison of jobs to determine their relative worth; basis for pay structure
Pay design; grade structure; resolving pay inequities

items: Structured/unstructured interviews with job holder and supervisor; flexible but time-consuming: Interview Method
Analyst directly observes employee performing work; accurate for manual jobs; not suitable for mental work: Observation Method
Position Analysis Questionnaire; standardised; quantitative; suitable for large organisations: Questionnaire Method (e.g., PAQ)
Employees record daily activities; useful for managerial jobs; respondent bias possible: Diary/Work Log Method
Identify critical behaviours that lead to success/failure; Flanagan's technique; competency identification: Critical Incident Technique (CIT)
Analyses what workers do in relation to data, people, and things; US DOL method: Functional Job Analysis (FJA)

blocks.content: Recruitment is the process of attracting, screening, and selecting qualified people for a job at an organisation or firm. It is a positive process :creating a pool of candidates from which selections are made.

cells: Promotions, transfers, rehires, employee referrals, internal job postings
Cost-effective; known performance; motivates existing employees; faster onboarding
Limited talent pool; inbreeding; may create internal politics
Campus recruitment, job portals (Naukri, LinkedIn), walk-in drives, employment exchanges, consultants/head-hunters, newspaper ads, social media
Fresh talent; new ideas; wider choice; specialised skills available
Higher cost; longer time; integration challenges; unknown performance

items: Online Job Boards: Naukri.com, LinkedIn, Indeed, Monster :post jobs and search resumes
Applicant Tracking System (ATS): Software to manage job applications; automate screening; IBPS uses ATS for banking recruitment
Social Media Recruiting: LinkedIn for professional hiring; Twitter, Instagram for employer branding
Video Interviewing: HireVue, Zoom interviews; especially post-COVID standard practice
AI in Recruitment: Resume parsing; chatbot screening; predictive hiring; bias concerns

rows: Searching for prospective employees and encouraging them to apply
Screening candidates and hiring the most suitable applicants
Does not result in an employment contract
Concludes with an offer letter/contract of employment

blocks.content: Selection is the process of choosing the most suitable candidate from the pool of applicants recruited. It is a negative process :eliminating unsuitable candidates :unlike recruitment which is positive.

cells: Brief interaction to check basic suitability; eliminate obviously unsuitable
Aptitude tests, technical tests, personality tests, SHL, NMAT; IBPS CWE for banking
Case GD; topic GD; fish bowl; abstract GD
Structured, semi-structured, unstructured; panel interview; stress interview
Check education, employment history, criminal record, references
Ensure fitness for the role; pre-employment health screening
Formal offer letter; negotiation; acceptance; joining formalities
Mechanical understanding; ability to work with machines
Specific knowledge and skills for the job
In-basket exercise; role play; case study presentation

items: Recruitment is classified as a 'positive process' (inviting candidates), whereas Selection is a 'negative process' (filtering out candidates).
Job Description focuses on the job duties and environment, while Job Specification focuses on human capabilities and qualifications.
Differentiate between Situational Interviews (hypothetical scenarios) and Behavioral Interviews (past actions and experiences).

cells: Pre-determined questions; same questions for all candidates; standardised scoring
Conversational; no fixed questions; flow based on candidate responses
Balance of standardisation and depth; most common
Deliberately challenging; create pressure situations; assess resilience
Jobs requiring high pressure performance; controversial method
Behavioural Event Interview; STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result)

blocks.content: Onboarding is the process of integrating a new employee into the organisation and acquainting them with the policies, culture, people, and their role. Effective onboarding improves retention, productivity, and employee engagement.

items: Pre-boarding: Document collection, IT setup, welcome email, buddy assignment before joining
Orientation: Company overview, vision/mission/values, policies, benefits, compliance training
Departmental Induction: Team introduction, role clarity, tools and systems, performance expectations
Buddy System: Senior employee assigned to guide new joinee informally for 3–6 months
30-60-90 Day Plan: Structured milestones for the first three months of employment
